bullets: How to draw bar models for word problems, with unit bars that are all the same length
slides.heading: The model method: bar models for word problems
slides.notes: Welcome everyone in and say: today we learn the model method - we draw a bar for each amount, split it into equal unit boxes, and let the model show us part-whole, before-and-after and difference problems before we calculate.

bullets: Draw unit bars: Mia has 2 units and Ben has 3 units, and every unit box is the same length
Use a before-and-after model: Mia starts with 3 units, gives 1 away and has 2 units left
Use a part-whole model: a class bar of 7 units splits into 3 boy-units and 4 girl-units
slides.heading: What we will learn
slides.notes: Read the three goals aloud and tell the class: keep these in mind, because the exit ticket at the end will ask you to draw a model and spot a model that is not to scale.

bullets: Sam draws a 1-unit bar and a 2-unit bar, but the 2-unit bar is not twice as long
Does the drawing still tell the truth, or has guessing the sizes broken the model?
slides.heading: Can this drawing be trusted?
slides.notes: Show Sam's two bars from scene s4 without the verdict first: ask for a show of hands on whether the drawing is fair, take two or three answers without judging them, and say scene s4 settles this exactly.

bullets: Each amount gets a bar, and the bar is split into unit boxes of exactly the same length
Because the units match, lengths in the drawing stand for amounts in the problem
slides.heading: A bar model is a scale drawing
slides.notes: Say this slowly, because it is the big idea of the whole lesson: the model only works if every unit box is the same length, so two units is exactly twice one unit.

bullets: Mia has 2 units and Ben has 3 units: Ben has one more unit box than Mia
The ruler checks every box: each unit box is the same length
slides.heading: Unit bars: every unit is the same length
slides.notes: Narrate the unit boxes sliding into place for Mia and then for Ben, then follow the ruler as it checks box after box and finds every length equal.

bullets: Before: Mia has 3 units; she gives 1 unit away to her sister
After: 2 units are left, because 3 - 1 = 2
slides.heading: Before-and-after: the model shows what changed
slides.notes: Watch the before bar of 3 units, follow the arrow as one unit moves away to her sister, then compare it with the after bar of 2 units sitting underneath.

bullets: The whole class bar has 7 units: 3 units are boys and 4 units are girls
The difference is the gap between the parts: diff = 4 - 3 = 1 unit
slides.heading: Worked example: part-whole and difference
slides.notes: Draw the whole bar first and split it into sevenths, mark 3 units as boys, then read off the girls as the other 4 units and find the difference of 1 unit.

bullets: Sam's 1-unit bar is drawn too long, so his 2-unit bar is not twice one unit
Drawn properly, the 2-unit bar is exactly twice the 1-unit bar: 2 units = 2 x 1 unit
slides.heading: Watch out: bars must be to scale
slides.notes: Hold Sam's bars up against the ruler to prove the units do not match, then compare them with the correct bars underneath, where the 2-unit bar is exactly twice the 1-unit bar.

bullets: Mia: 2 units, Ben: 3 units, and every unit box is the same length
Line the bars up and count the gap: Ben has 1 more unit than Mia
slides.heading: Worked example: how many more units does Ben have?
slides.notes: Talk through the unit-bar working slowly as in scene s1 and name each step: draw both bars with equal unit boxes first, then compare their lengths.

bullets: Draw a before-and-after model for: Ana has 4 units and gives 1 away. How many units are left?
Draw a part-whole bar of 5 units where 2 units are red pens. How many units are not red pens?
slides.heading: Your turn: draw it before you work it out
slides.notes: Give pairs three minutes, then cold-call one pair on each part: press them on drawing every unit box the same length before they write any numbers.

bullets: On your own: draw a bar model with equal unit boxes for a short word problem
Explain in one sentence why unit boxes must all be the same length
slides.heading: Exit ticket: show what you know
slides.notes: Collect these before anyone leaves and say: I am looking for unit boxes that are all the same length in your drawing, plus one clear sentence about scale in your explanation.
